import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate 'Total_Spending' by summing up all product spending columns
spending_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt') and col.endswith('Products') or col == 'MntWines' or col == 'MntGoldProds']
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Handle missing 'Income' values by dropping rows with NaN in 'Income'
# This is important for numerical plots involving income
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Map 'Response' column to more descriptive labels for the legend
df['Response_Label'] = df['Response'].map({0: 'No', 1: 'Yes'})

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Response_Label',  # Color points based on campaign response
    style='Response_Label', # Use different markers for different responses
    alpha=0.7,             # Slightly transparent points
    s=100,                 # Adjust point size
    palette='viridis'      # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Income vs. Total Spending by Campaign Response', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)

# Improve the legend
plt.legend(title='Responded to Last Campaign', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='10')

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
